:::{#sol-expected-density}

**Part 1.**
Apply @thm-lotus, continuous case, with $g(x) = \p(X=x)$:

$$
\ba
\E{\p(X=X)}
&= \int_{x \in \rangef{X}} \p(X=x) \cd \p(X=x)\,dx
&& \text{(LOTUS, continuous case, with } g(x) = \p(X=x) \text{)}
\\&= \int_{x \in \rangef{X}} \sb{\p(X=x)}^2\,dx.
&& \text{(combine the two factors)}
\ea
$$

The expectation of the density is the integral of the squared density.
It is large when the density is concentrated,
because then $X$ tends to land where the density is high.

**Part 2.**
The density is $\p(X=x) = \tfrac{1}{b-a}$ on $[a, b]$ and $0$ elsewhere:

$$
\ba
\E{\p(X=X)}
&= \int_a^b \paren{\frac{1}{b-a}}^2\,dx
&& \text{(Part 1; the density is } 0 \text{ outside } [a, b] \text{)}
\\&= \frac{1}{(b-a)^2} \cd (b-a)
&& \text{(the integrand is constant on an interval of length } b-a \text{)}
\\&= \frac{1}{b-a}.
&& \text{(cancel one factor of } b-a \text{)}
\ea
$$

Here the density is constant, so $\p(X=X) = \tfrac{1}{b-a}$ with certainty, and its expectation is the same value.

**Part 3.**
The density is $\p(X=x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\ss}}\exp\paren{-\frac{(x-\mean)^2}{2\ss}}$:

$$
\ba
\E{\p(X=X)}
&= \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2\pi\ss}\exp\paren{-\frac{(x-\mean)^2}{\ss}}\,dx
&& \text{(Part 1; square the density)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2\pi\ss} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-u^2}\,\sigma\,du
&& \text{(substitute } u = (x-\mean)/\sigma \text{, so } dx = \sigma\,du \text{)}
\\&= \frac{\sigma\sqrt{\pi}}{2\pi\ss}
&& \text{(the given integral)}
\\&= \frac{1}{2\sigma\sqrt{\pi}}.
&& \text{(simplify, using } \ss = \sigma^2 \text{)}
\ea
$$

A larger [standard deviation](#def-sd) $\sigma$ spreads the density out and lowers its expected value.

:::
